meta.important_document_change: There is NO 'Pricing Arrangements and Price Limits 2026-27' (PAPL). For 2026-27 the NDIA published a prices-only 'NDIS Pricing Schedule 2026-27' (effective 1 July 2026, v1.2), which was replaced by the Minister's pricing determination Schedule effective 24 September 2026. Claiming rules (travel, km rates) not restated in the Schedules are taken from the PAPL 2025-26 v1.1, which the NDIS pricing page still lists as a current guidance document.

time_bands.applicability_note: Schedule Part 1 s2.4(b): 'A provider may claim up to the maximum amount for a support item in Appendices 1, 2 and 3 that references the day of the week or the time of the day in accordance with the definitions in Part 4.' (PDF p5)

definitions_verbatim.weekday: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday (unless the day is a public holiday).
definitions_verbatim.weekday_daytime: Any support to a participant that starts at or after 6:00 am and ends before or at 8:00 pm on a single weekday (unless it is a Public Holiday or Night-time Sleepover Support).
definitions_verbatim.weekday_evening: Any support to a participant that starts at or after 8:00 pm and finishes at or before midnight on a single weekday (unless it is a Public Holiday or Night-time Sleepover Support).
definitions_verbatim.weekday_night: Any support to a participant that commences at or before midnight on a weekday and finishes after midnight on the next weekday, or commences before 6:00 am on a weekday and finishes on that weekday (unless it is a Public Holiday, Saturday, Sunday or Night-time Sleepover Support).
definitions_verbatim.saturday: Any support to a participant that starts at or after midnight on the night prior to a Saturday and ends before or at midnight of that Saturday (unless it is a Public Holiday or Night-time Sleepover Support).
definitions_verbatim.sunday: Any support to a participant that starts at or after midnight on the night prior to a Sunday and ends before or at midnight of that Sunday (unless it is a Public Holiday or Night-time Sleepover Support).
definitions_verbatim.public_holiday_support: Any support to a participant that starts at or after midnight on the night prior to a Public Holiday and ends before or at midnight of that Public Holiday (unless it is a Night-time Sleepover Support).
definitions_verbatim.public_holiday_days: Any of the following days: 1 January (New Year's Day); 26 January (Australia Day); Good Friday; Easter Monday; 25 April (Anzac Day); King's birthday holiday (the day on which it is celebrated in a State or Territory or a region of a State or Territory); 25 December (Christmas Day); 26 December (Boxing Day); any other day or part-day declared as a public holiday within a State or Territory where the support is being delivered.
definitions_verbatim.night_time_sleepover_support: Any support to a participant which is delivered on a weekday, a Saturday, a Sunday or a Public Holiday that: Commences before midnight on a day and finishes after midnight on that day; and Is for a continuous period of eight (8) hours or more; and The worker is allowed to sleep when they are not providing support; and Where more than two (2) hours of active support is provided, a provider may claim for the third or additional hour at Saturday rates on weekdays, or at applicable rates on other days (Saturday, Sunday or Public Holidays).

time_bands.papl_2025_26_wording_difference: PAPL 2025-26 v1.1 (PDF p18) Weekday Night wording differs slightly: 'commences at or before midnight on a weekday and finishes after midnight on that weekday, or commences before 6:00 am on a weekday and finishes on that weekday'. The 2026-27 Schedule says 'finishes after midnight on the next weekday'. Daytime and Evening wording is identical in both documents.
time_bands.evening_starts_at_8pm_note: Per the verbatim definitions, Weekday Evening is a support that STARTS at or after 8:00 pm. A weekday support that starts before 8:00 pm and ends after 8:00 pm meets neither the Daytime nor the Evening definition, so it is a boundary-crossing support (see boundary_rule).

boundary_rule.rule_2026_27_verbatim: Where a support a support crosses between different times of day or days of week and is delivered by a single worker, the higher of the amounts applies to the whole support.

rule_2026_27_source.where: Part 1: Maximum amounts, section 2.4 'Day and time', paragraph (c), PDF page 5 of 96 (the duplicated words 'a support a support' are in the official PDF and DOCX)

boundary_rule.rule_2025_26_verbatim: If a support to a participant does not meet one of the above criteria, then it needs to be billed as two or more separate supports. An exception to this general rule occurs when a particular support crosses a shift boundary and the same worker delivers the entire support. In this case, the higher of the relevant price limits applies to the entire support and the provider should make the claim against the relevant support item. Providers are required to discuss this billing arrangement with the participant.

rule_2025_26_source.where: General Claiming Rules > Time of Day and Day of Week, PDF page 18 of 104 (section begins p17); identical wording in v1.0

boundary_rule.summary_for_code: Single worker, support crosses a time-of-day or day-of-week boundary: claim the WHOLE support against the item for the higher-priced band (not split). The 2025-26 PAPL says that otherwise (i.e. not the same worker for the whole support) the support is billed as two or more separate supports. The 2026-27 Schedule states only the single-worker rule; it does not restate the split rule.
boundary_rule.unverified: The 2026-27 Schedule does not say what happens when the higher band has no item for that support (e.g. a community-access support running past midnight on a weekday: there is no 'Access Community Social and Rec Activ - Standard - Weekday Night' item). Not resolved by any official text found.

provider_travel_time_labour.how_claimed: Travel time is claimed against the same support item as the primary support, using the 'Provider Travel' claim type; catalogue column 'Provider Travel' = 'Y' for all 11 items above.
provider_travel_time_labour.time_cap_rule_one_sentence: In MMM1-3 areas a provider can claim up to 30 minutes of travel time to and from each participant (up to 60 minutes in MMM4-5), for each eligible worker; the MMM class is based on where the participant is when the support is delivered.
provider_travel_time_labour.time_cap_verbatim: When a provider claims for labour costs (travel time) related to a support, they can claim for up to 30 minutes of travel to and from each participant in MMM1-3 areas and up to 60 minutes in MMM4-5 areas for each eligible worker. This is known as a travel time limit.
provider_travel_time_labour.rate_rule_verbatim: The hourly rate for travel claims should be the same as the rate agreed for the primary support, or lower if agreed with the participant.
provider_travel_time_labour.sole_trader_condition_verbatim: The provider is required to pay the worker delivering the support for the time spent travelling because of the agreement under which the worker is employed; or the provider is a sole trader and is travelling from their usual place of work to or from the participant, or between participants.
provider_travel_time_labour.return_travel_verbatim: In addition to the above travel, providers delivering core and capacity-building supports can also claim for travel time from the last participant to their usual place of work but only if they must pay their worker for the return travel time and this is subject to the relevant travel time limit.
provider_travel_time_labour.prior_agreement_verbatim: The participant has agreed to the travel costs in advance (that is, the Agreement between the participant and provider should specify the travel costs that can be claimed)

sources.where: General Claiming Rules > Provider Travel (PDF p21-22) and Provider Travel - Labour Costs (Time) (PDF p22)

s12 Isolated Towns (PDF p172): restates 'In MM 1-3 areas providers can claim up to 30 minutes of travel (labour time) to and from each participant. In MM 4-5 locations providers can claim up to 60 minutes'

gst.verbatim: Any maximum amount specified in this document already includes any Goods and Services Tax (GST).

other_rules.who_limits_apply_to_verbatim: the maximum amounts specified in Part 2 apply to the acquisition or provision of an NDIS support or class of NDIS supports if the funding for the support or class of supports under a participant's plan is managed by: i. The National Disability Insurance Agency (NDIA) (Agency-managed); or ii. A registered plan management provider (plan managed).
other_rules.geography_verbatim: If a support is delivered in a MM 1-5 location, except for areas reclassified under Part 3 - Isolated Towns Modification - Type 1, the national amount applies.

ttp.statement: No Temporary Transformation Payment (TTP) items or TTP loading appear in either 2026-27 Pricing Schedule, the 2026-27 Support Catalogue (current or legacy sheet), or the PAPL 2025-26 text (0 matches for 'TTP'/'Transformation Payment'). The APR 2026-27 (Table 44, PDF p139) lists residual payments Jul-Dec 2025 against 'Access Community Social and Recreational Activities Standard - TTP' ($1.3m) and 'Group Activities Standard - TTP' ($0.5m); why those claims exist (e.g. late claims for earlier dates) is not stated and was not verified.

sources.where: Table 44, PDF p139

unregistered_sole_traders.one_sentence: As at 13 Oct 2026, the binding 2026-27 maximum amounts make no registered/unregistered distinction (they apply to Agency-managed and plan-managed funding, Schedule Part 1 s1.1), and the PAPL 2025-26 says plan managers must keep providers within the price limits 'regardless of whether the participant purchases the support from a registered or an unregistered provider' (PDF p10); so an unregistered sole trader may charge plan-managed participants up to the same limits, but Agency-managed supports require a Registered Provider (PAPL PDF p9).
unregistered_sole_traders.verbatim_papl_p10: Plan managers must adhere to the arrangements prescribed in the NDIS Pricing Arrangements and Price Limits, including ensuring that the prices charged by providers do not exceed the price limits. This rule applies regardless of whether the participant purchases the support from a registered or an unregistered provider.
unregistered_sole_traders.verbatim_papl_p9_agency_managed: A provider of a support that is agency managed in a participant's plan: Must be a Registered Provider with the NDIS;
unregistered_sole_traders.verbatim_papl_p10_self_managed: Self-managing participants can use registered or unregistered providers and are not subject to the price limits or other pricing arrangements set out in the NDIS Pricing Arrangements and Price Limits and its associated documents.
unregistered_sole_traders.pending_change: APR 2026-27 Recommendation 16 (PDF p13): 'The prices for Social, Community and Civic Participation supports delivered by unregistered providers, including high intensity supports should be reduced by 10% from 1 January 2027.' The 24 Sep 2026 media release says the government is 'currently consulting' on differentiated pricing. NOT yet in force; check for an updated Schedule before 1 Jan 2027. If adopted, it would affect 04_10x_0125_6_1 items for unregistered sole traders.
